## Overview

Report supported MTP prediction-layer reuse at INFO and link to actionable speculative-depth tuning guidance. Fixes #62640.

## Claims

- Depths above one no longer produce the existing acceptance-rate warning.
- The diagnostic and documentation explain using accepted draft tokens together with end-to-end latency or throughput.
- Configuration, depth thresholds, model-family exclusions, and inference behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

Using real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` metadata and the public `ModelConfig`/`SpeculativeConfig` constructors on Linux ARM64:

| Depth | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | No reuse diagnostic | No reuse diagnostic |
| 3 | WARNING, acceptance-rate caveat | INFO, tuning guidance and documentation link |

Both configurations resolve to `deepseek_mtp` with the same configured depth and configuration hash before/after. No model weights are loaded for this logging-only validation.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/config/test_bailing_mtp_config.py \
  tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py -q
```

19 tests passed. Pre-commit and MkDocs build passed. No throughput improvement is claimed or benchmarked, and full MTP GPU inference was not exercised.

<details>
<summary>Diagnostic reproduction</summary>

```python
from vllm.config import ModelConfig, ParallelConfig, SpeculativeConfig
from vllm.config.logging import LoggingConfig
from vllm.logger import configure_logging

configure_logging(LoggingConfig())
target = ModelConfig(model="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3", enforce_eager=True)
for depth in (1, 3):
    print(SpeculativeConfig(
        method="mtp",
        num_speculative_tokens=depth,
        target_model_config=target,
        target_parallel_config=ParallelConfig(),
    ))
```

</details>

## Details

The warning treated a supported configuration as exceptional without telling users how to evaluate it. Keep the existing condition and give a concise information message with a link to guidance: compare depths and a no-speculation baseline on the same workload, and use acceptance counters as supporting measurements. The docs link to recipes and per-request metrics. They deliberately avoid a universal acceptance-rate target because a higher rate alone does not imply better latency or throughput.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-10-21 found no open PR addressing #62640 or the MTP warning/tuning guidance.

AI assistance: Codex helped implement the diagnostic, documentation, and validation.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -83,3 +83,28 @@ vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-7B-Base \
   per lm_head weight, e.g. 0.6 or 0.35 GiB for a 248k x 2560 head; it is
   counted in the model weights, so with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` leave room
   for it.
+
+## Tuning Speculative Depth
+
+`num_speculative_tokens` sets the maximum number of tokens drafted per step.
+Values greater than `1` are supported. When additional steps reuse MTP prediction
+layers, vLLM logs an informational tuning message; this is not a configuration
+error. More draft tokens can increase the number accepted per step, but also add
+drafting and verification work. The best depth depends on the model, hardware,
+prompts, and request concurrency.
+
+Start with the relevant [vLLM recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/), when available,
+and compare several depths on the same workload. Measure end-to-end latency or
+throughput against both a smaller depth and a run without speculative decoding.
+Choose the setting that improves the metric your deployment needs.
+
+The `/metrics` endpoint exposes `vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total` and
+`vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total`. Divide their increases over the same
+measurement interval to obtain the draft-token acceptance rate. Use
+`vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total` to compare accepted tokens per verification
+step. The [per-request acceptance metrics](acceptance_metrics.md) provide the same
+information for individual requests.
+
+Acceptance rate alone does not measure speedup: a smaller depth can have a higher
+acceptance rate while producing fewer accepted tokens per step. There is no
+universal target acceptance percentage or depth that is optimal for all models.
